analysis:
The PR modifies only docs/architecture/inference.md; there are no code, config or deployment changes. The supplied units are BASE text for lines 1-797, where the base-side changed range is only lines 1087-1088. The visible head changes are documentation of CBv2 prefill geometry (wider 2048/4096 chunk for GPT-OSS, dense Qwen3.5/3.8 and Gemma 4; a 512 media chunk ceiling; no solo stripe for GPT-OSS and Gemma 4) and further edits at head lines 1100-1146 and 2028-2041. Those lines were not supplied and the patch excerpt is truncated, so I could not examine them.

From the base text I checked the security-relevant statements against T-041, which covers the prefix cache and the SSD tier:
- Cache scope is the authenticated tenant scope, and it is off without one.
- Super's checkpoint bank is partitioned by that scope.
- The documented TTL and disk behavior is unchanged.
- The Super managed slot emits no cache receipts.

Nothing in the supplied base text weakens any of these statements, and I found no changed statement that conflicts with the T-041 sign-off conditions (30-minute TTL, authenticated account isolation, HMAC names). Documenting a wider prefill chunk could affect memory admission and DoS posture (T-029, T-010), and the prefix-cache sign-off is also sensitive to chunk geometry, since Super's prefix checkpoints sit at chunk multiples. Whether the real code matches the documented geometry cannot be confirmed from this docs-only change.

Open questions for the integration pass: whether the wider chunk and step defaults in EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift (prefillGeometry) are covered by memory-admission checks; and whether the unseen head hunks at 1100-1146 and 2028-2041 alter any cache-scope, TTL or authorization claims. No concrete regression is established from the supplied evidence.
